citation.authors: Powell W, Adams LB, Cole-Lewis Y et al

cited_by.title: Black men, depression and getting support

record.population: 458 African American men, recruited mainly from US barbershops
record.design: Cross-sectional survey and path analysis of barriers to help-seeking
record.finding: More frequent everyday racism and higher masculinity norm salience went with higher barriers to health help-seeking. Everyday racism's link to barriers was partly explained by a lower sense of control and more depressive symptoms. The authors say interventions should address masculinity norms and also threats to sense of control and the effects of everyday racism.
record.note: One cross-sectional survey in US barbershops; cannot show cause. Abstract read.
